project.title: Bluetooth Race Car
project.goal: A beginner-buildable, battery-powered, two-motor differential-drive race car controlled over Bluetooth LE.

requirements.label: Two independently controlled brushed DC motors
Hobbyist prototype build with boards and modules

outputV.note: Single 5 V rail shared by the XIAO VBUS input and the motor driver

assumptions.reason: 3S instead of the handoff's 2S: with a series Schottky and a 5 V LM2596 output, 2S leaves under 1 V of regulator headroom at end of discharge. 3S keeps about 4 V. Exact pack and connector deferred.
Simple, through-hole, protects the buck and everything downstream; costs about 0.45 V that 3S can afford
One buck output feeds both the XIAO 5V input and the driver motor rail. Motors are 6 V nominal, so this trades roughly 17 percent top speed for one regulator.
Heuristic bulk capacitance on the shared 5 V rail to soften motor start and stall transients. Not a component-spec invariant.
Per motor, averaged over a mixed drive cycle at about 40 percent duty. Runtime estimate depends on this.
XIAO ESP32-S3 with BLE active, no Wi-Fi
Typical for an LM2596 module at this ratio and load

assumptions.value: D0-D5 to PWMA, AIN1, AIN2, PWMB, BIN1, BIN2; D6 to STBY
assumptions.reason: Arbitrary; any PWM-capable XIAO GPIO works

mutations.label: What if there is no battery?
mutations.description: Deletes the battery instance and clears the power source. The project becomes incomplete and voltage-dependent rules stop evaluating.

mutations.label: What if the driver's ground is broken?
mutations.description: Moves the driver GND pin onto its own net. The driver still receives 5 V and control signals but shares no reference with the XIAO.

mutations.label: What if STBY is tied to ground?
mutations.description: Moves the driver STBY pin from the XIAO GPIO to GND. The driver is held in standby.

mutations.label: What if STBY is left unconnected?
mutations.description: Disconnects STBY entirely. On this exact Adafruit breakout the 10 kOhm pull-up keeps the driver enabled, so no finding is expected.

mutations.label: What if a motor is wired to a GPIO?
mutations.description: Moves the left motor off the driver and onto XIAO D7 and D8.

mutations.label: What if the buck is set to 3.3 V?
mutations.description: Changes the buck module output. The driver motor supply minimum is 4.5 V and the XIAO 5V input expects about 5 V.

mutations.label: What if the buck is set to 14 V?
mutations.description: Exceeds the driver's 13.5 V motor supply maximum and the XIAO 5V input.

mutations.label: Remove reverse-polarity protection
mutations.description: Deletes the diode and wires the battery straight into the buck. The circuit still runs; the reverse-polarity strategy is gone.

mutations.label: Remove the bulk capacitor
mutations.description: Deletes the 470 uF capacitor from the 5 V rail. Heuristic rule; expect a warning, not a failure.

mutations.label: What if the battery is 2S?
mutations.description: Uses the handoff's original 2S class. With the series diode, the buck sees about 5.95 V at end of discharge for a 5 V output.

mutations.label: What if a motor stalls at 2.5 A?
mutations.description: Replaces the left motor with a class whose stall current exceeds the driver's 1.2 A continuous limit.

mutations.label: What if the driver is a bare IC?
mutations.description: Replaces the Adafruit breakout with the bare Toshiba IC. Same limits, but no onboard decoupling and no STBY pull-up.

findings.title: TB6612 motor driver is held in standby
findings.consequence: Both H-bridges are disabled. The board receives commands and PWM but neither motor turns. Drive is unavailable.
remediation: Move the pin to a GPIO and drive it high in firmware
Tie it to the logic rail
Leave it unconnected: this breakout's pull-up enables the driver by default

findings.title: Estimated runtime 183 min is 6.1x the 30 min target: the battery may be larger, heavier, and costlier than the goal needs
findings.consequence: Electrically valid, but the pack is sized well beyond the stated runtime target. Excess capacity costs mass, volume, and money in a small car.
remediation: Right-size the battery toward the target with the Optimize step
Or raise the runtime target if longer sessions are the real goal

findings.title: Motors run at 5.00 V, below their 6.00 V rating: about 17 percent lower no-load speed (estimated)
findings.consequence: Top speed and torque are below what the motors can deliver. Brushed DC no-load speed scales roughly with voltage; torque and current scale with it too, so a higher rail also raises stall current and runtime cost.
remediation: Raise the motor rail toward the rating with the Optimize step, keeping the logic supply within its own range
Or accept the lower speed for the runtime and simplicity it buys
